Cache latency vs working set · cycles

Each cliff is a cache running out of room — the memory hierarchy drawn by a stopwatch. "Is my data in cache?" usually matters more than the algorithm.

Core scaling · G/s vs threads

Peak 318 G/s, 15× one core. 24 = 32 threads exactly — there's no 19th core to run on.

Bandwidth vs threads · GB/s

Maxed by ~6 cores. Compute scales to 18, bandwidth doesn't — the line between "more cores help" and "more cores wasted."

Disk read vs block · GB/s

~100× faster from block size alone — bigger reads amortize the per-call syscall cost.

GPU TFLOP/s vs threads

Peak 14.9 TF, but only once fed ~250k threads; below that it's slower than the CPU.

★ It all comes down to two knobs

independence — is there other work to overlap while you wait? A dependency chain pins you to 1×; independent work buys ~6–20×. It showed up everywhere — dependent vs independent adds, instruction layout, streaming loads, the FMA ceiling.
locality — is the data reachable cheaply? Up to ~100× between L1 and a random DRAM miss, and the prefetcher erases the size penalty entirely when your access pattern is predictable.
Multiply them: ~2,000× between best-case compute and a random DRAM miss, ~300,000× down to the SSD. Which end your code lands on is mostly data layout and access order, not instruction count.
